malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code imports a JavaScript file from a remote domain (fonts.googleapis.com) into the application template, allowing remote content to be loaded and potentially replaced with malicious code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Importing executable content (JavaScript or CSS) from an external, uncontrolled domain can allow attackers to inject or replace content with malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal application templates should only load trusted, vetted resources or self-hosted assets. Loading from external domains, especially those not under organizational control, increases the attack surface.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use includes loading fonts or scripts from trusted CDNs, but only when the CDN is trusted and the risk is understood.
key_indicators: Remote domain not under organizational control
Potential for content replacement or injection

attack_chain.action: Application template loads external resource from a remote domain at runtime.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential for attacker to replace or inject malicious code via the external resource.

behavioral_signatures: Importing or requiring executable content (JavaScript, CSS) from remote domains in application templates or code
References to external domains in HTML, JavaScript, or configuration files
file_indicators: templates/*.html with <script> or <link> tags referencing external domains
Configuration files or code referencing non-whitelisted domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not under organizational control (e.g., fonts.googleapis.com, untrusted CDNs)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan application templates and code for <script> or <link> tags referencing external domains. Monitor runtime network activity for outbound requests to non-whitelisted domains. Flag any executable content loaded from remote sources not explicitly approved by security policy.
